name: manual_90fcf8
claim: When a bash script pipes an external tool through '2>/dev/null || true' inside a scan loop, a missing binary (not just a missing match) silently produces zero hits — always guard with 'command -v <tool>' before the loop, and never trust an environment-isolation fix as root cause until CI itself confirms it against a captured execution trace

decisions.notes: Diagnosed orama-system PR #298: tests/test_scan_tracked_banned_tokens.py failed only on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, passing identically in 3 local/sandboxed environments. First hypothesis (ambient os.environ.copy() contamination) was fixed and pushed but CI still failed identically -- proved the hypothesis wrong instead of re-claiming success. Root cause found only after adding real bash -x trace + targeted rg --debug/--no-ignore instrumentation and reading the actual CI log: ripgrep was never installed on the runner, and scan-tracked-banned-tokens.sh's 'rg ... 2>/dev/null || true' pattern silently swallowed the resulting FileNotFoundError-equivalent (rg: command not found), so the scan reported clean having never actually searched. A second landmine surfaced mid-fix: the repo's own CI bootstrap script used the literal placeholder pattern 'REDACTED' for its intentionally-inert CI-only pattern file (real banned-token registries are local-only by design, never present in CI) -- installing ripgrep would have made that placeholder real for the first time and mass-failed CI, since 'REDACTED' is a common word in genuine security/redaction docs. Fixed by using a synthetic sentinel built via string concatenation (so the sentinel's own literal text doesn't appear in tracked source and self-flag).
